ADVANCED SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH
What is ‘Advanced Scientific Research’?

Advanced Scientific Research' refers to the process in which a student, typically in grades 8-12, will identify a topic of their own choosing based on their own personal interests and curiosity and will develop an authentic research project to answer an original research question across fields spanning Natural Sciences, Technology & Engineering, Social Sciences, Business & Finance,... Working alongside expert mentors, students formulate their research question, design a methodology, collect and analyze data, and produce findings that are entirely their own. These findings are then written up as an academic paper and presented at local, national, and international science competitions and symposia with standout projects moving forward to publication in peer-reviewed journals.

At GSJ, we recognize that the most powerful driver behind every great research project is a student's genuine curiosity and passion for discovery and our scientific research program is built to channel exactly that into real, publishable, competition-ready work.
Our Science Research Overview

- Mentorship
Students are grouped into team (4-6 members) or potentially paired with professional scientists who act as their mentors throughout the program. The mentors provide guidance, knowledge, and support as the student undertakes research. 

- Research Report
Upon completion of their research, students are required to write an academic-level research paper detailing their methodology, results, and conclusions following standard scientific format and guidelines.

- Presentation
Students showcase their findings before a panel of experts at GSJ, various competitions, symposia, and science fairs at national and international levels. This provides them with the opportunity to communicate their research effectively and receive feedback from peers and professionals in the field.

- Publication
Exceptional research projects have the chance to be published in scientific journals, thereby contributing meaningfully to the scientific community. Moreover, students stand a chance to win accolades and recognition for their exemplary work through competitions and symposia.
Why Participate?

- Fosters Curiosity & Creativity
Scientific research encourages students to explore their curiosity, think outside the box, and come up with innovative solutions to complex problems.

- Hands-On Experience
Students gain practical experience in scientific research, learning essential skills in critical thinking, problem-solving, data analysis, and scientific writing.

- Professional Networking
By working closely with a mentor, students build valuable connections within the scientific community, opening doors to future opportunities in academia and industry. Students also learn to work collaboratively with peers and supervisors in a professional setting.

- Skill Development
The program hones students' skills in research design, experimentation, data interpretation, and presentation, laying a solid foundation for their future academic and professional pursuits.

- Enhances University Applications
Participation in scientific research demonstrates to university admissions officers a student's passion for learning, ability to work independently, and dedication to a particular field of study, giving applicants a competitive edge during the university admissions process.

Research Process

1. Choose Topic
The first step is choosing a topic to study that you have a personal interest or curiosity about.

2. Develop Research Question: Tìm kiếm & đọc các tài liệu tham khảo, chỉ ra khoảng trống nghiên cứu từ đó phát triển research question

3. Create Research Plan: 
At this point, you will create a research plan prior to starting your study.

4. Conduct Research
Students will conduct their research following the methodology they outlined in their research plan.

5. Conduct Analysis & Draw Conclusions
Students will analyze the data collected in their methodology to draw conclusions.

6. Present Findings
Write an report & presentation to share your findings with the world!

Become A Mentors
Become a Mentor with GSJ

At GSJ, mentors play a vital role in shaping the next generation of scientists, innovators, and thinkers. Our team brings together experts from diverse academic institutions and professional backgrounds worldwide, each committed to nurturing curiosity and scientific literacy. Beyond guiding a single research project, our mentors inspire students and share their expertise across a wide range of fields. If you are passionate about research and believe in the power of mentorship, we invite you to join our growing community at GSJ.
Benefits for Mentors

- Meaningful Impact: Directly contribute to a young scholar's academic growth, confidence, and future opportunities.

- Professional Development: Gain valuable teaching and mentorship experience that strengthens your professional profile.

- Networking & Recognition: Join a growing community of scientists, educators, and professionals at GSJ committed to expanding access to authentic research experiences.

- Stipend: Receive a stipend per student to compensate you for your time and any expenses incurred throughout the research process.

- Flexible Engagement: Work with students remotely or in-person based on your availability and field.

- Professional Support & Guidance: Receive dedicated support from GSJ staff with extensive experience guiding high school students through research projects.
What do we provide?

- GSJ provides mentors with a dedicated workspace on Zoom to conduct mentoring sessions, with scheduling support handled by our team to ensure a smooth and hassle-free experience.

- Mentors can easily monitor student progress, assign tasks and milestones, communicate with their student, and review submitted materials such as research plans, abstracts, data, and research papers throughout the process.

- Students are supported by GSJ's team of dedicated teaching assistants with extensive experience guiding high school students through research projects, ensuring they remain on track every step of the way.

- GSJ staff are always available to address any questions or concerns that arise, providing responsive and attentive support to both mentors and students throughout the program.
Expectation & Require

- Guide students through the research process by sharing your knowledge, providing constructive feedback, and offering expertise in your field.

- Meet regularly with your mentee to review progress, discuss findings, and work through any challenges that arise.

- Review and provide feedback on data analysis, paper drafts, and presentations as the project approaches completion.

- Maintain open communication with GSJ staff to support student progress and uphold academic integrity throughout the program.

- Hold at least a bachelor's degree in a relevant field across Natural Sciences, Technology, Engineering, Social Sciences, or Business (graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and working professionals are welcome).
Time Commitment

- Research engagements can be conducted remotely or in-person, depending on the nature of each research project.

- Mentors are expected to commit to a 5 to 6 month engagement, with one session of approximately 2.5 to 3 hours per week per project.

- As most research projects are conducted in person, we kindly ask that mentors confirm their availability to participate on-site before joining the program.

Do Hoang Minh Tue - Nearly US$400,000 in scholarships from leading universities worldwide (NUS, UVA, UGA, UConn, USF, University of Melbourne, VinUniversity, ...)

Looking back on my high school years, what has shaped me the most was not only exams or grades, but also my experience working on research project at GSJ.

Before this project, I had participated in several smaller research activities, but mostly at an introductory level. It was only through hands-on experimental research that I began to understand the level of persistence and pressure that laboratory work requires.

To optimize the product, my team continuously tested different conditions, including strip-drying temperatures and gold nanoparticle incubation times. During some stages, we spent multiple sessions assembling dozens to hundreds of test kits, followed by spectral measurements and result evaluations. Although the repetitive nature of the work could sometimes be demanding, it also taught me how to stay focused and work more systematically.

Throughout the process, I received significant support from the teachers and mentors at GSJ. From shaping the research direction and refining the procedure to providing technical guidance during experiments, their support motivated me to stay committed to the project. Being introduced to research early on and having clear guidance also helped me feel more confident when presenting my academic journey during university applications.

What I found most meaningful was how scientific research transformed learning from something purely theoretical into a practical experience. Instead of only studying concepts from textbooks, I had the opportunity to test hypotheses directly through real data and experimental results.

By the end of this journey, what I gained was not only a completed research project, but also stronger working skills, better time management, and a more proactive mindset as I prepare for university life ahead.

Yes. Student is paired with a qualified mentor from an academic institution or professional background relevant to their research field.

6. Does GSJ offer study abroad consulting?
Yes. GSJ provides personalized study abroad consulting, supporting students with profile building, essay writing, university selection, and application preparation.

7. What competitions can students participate in through GSJ?
GSJ prepares students for a wide range of local and international competitions, including iCAN, SVIIF, iWISE, ABS, and various scientific research symposia.

Yes. GSJ organizes international career exploration camps and summer programs in destinations such as Singapore and Australia,America,... designed to broaden students' academic horizons and expand their global network.

GSJ designs individualized academic roadmaps based on each student's strengths, interests, and goals, ensuring guidance that is relevant and meaningful to their personal journey.

You can reach out to our team via our website or contact us directly to schedule a one-on-one consultation. Our staff will help identify the most suitable program for your child.

What Does It Take to Build a Competitive University Application?

Strong grades may open doors, but they rarely tell the whole story. Leading U.S. universities consider academic readiness, intellectual curiosity, extracurricular commitment, personal character, and potential contributions.
76.8% of surveyed colleges rated grades in college-preparatory courses as considerably important.
63.8% rated the strength of the high school curriculum as considerably important.
Source: National Association for College Admission Counseling (NACAC)

What Harvard Says
 “There is no formula for gaining admission to Harvard.”
 Harvard explains that its admissions process considers not only academic accomplishment, but also leadership, community involvement, extracurricular distinction, and personal character.
 Source: Harvard

A compelling application is not a collection of impressive credentials. It is a coherent reflection of a student’s abilities, interests, values, and potential.
 
 At GSJ, we help students develop these qualities through a structured, personalized mentoring journey.
From Self-Discovery to University Success: Your Journey with GSJ

Every student begins with different strengths, aspirations, and circumstances. That is why GSJ does not believe in one-size-fits-all application strategies.
 
 Our mentoring approach brings together six interconnected stages, helping students make informed decisions, pursue meaningful experiences, and present their achievements with clarity and authenticity.

01. Self-Discovery & Career Exploration
 
02. Academic Excellence & Intellectual Development
 
03. Research, Extracurricular Activities & Leadership
 
04. University Selection & Admissions Strategy
 
05. Application Preparation, Essays & Interviews
 
06. Post-Admission Support & University Transition
Discover your strengths. Find your direction.

Before choosing a university or major, students need to understand their interests, motivations, abilities, and long-term aspirations.
 
 Universities such as Yale value intellectual curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to explore new ideas. Yale's admissions framework explicitly considers academic potential, contributions to others, and openness to new horizons.

Students may feel pressured to choose a prestigious or popular major without fully understanding what studying or working in that field involves. Others have multiple interests but struggle to identify a direction that genuinely fits their strengths.

Step 1: Personal Assessment
 Explore interests, personality traits, academic strengths, and career preferences through structured assessments and individual conversations.
 
 Step 2: Expert Career Mentoring
 Meet with GSJ mentors and relevant subject specialists to explore potential majors, career pathways, and industry expectations.
 
 Step 3: Real-World Career Exploration
 Discover what different fields involve through academic workshops, practical projects, university visits, and relevant experiential learning opportunities.
 
 Step 4: Personalized Career Roadmap
 Identify promising academic directions and develop an actionable plan that connects present interests with future university and career goals.
 
 Outcome: A clearer understanding of personal strengths, potential majors, and future career pathways.
Build the academic foundation to thrive at university.

Academic performance remains a cornerstone of competitive university admissions. Admissions committees evaluate not only grades but also the rigor of coursework, consistency of achievement, and readiness for advanced study.
 Yale describes the high school transcript as the single most important document in its application review.

Balancing demanding schoolwork, international qualifications, standardized tests, and extracurricular commitments can be overwhelming. Without a clear strategy, students may invest time in credentials that do not meaningfully support their university goals.

1. Academic Profile Evaluation - Review transcripts, course selections, academic performance, and existing qualifications to identify strengths and development priorities.
 
 2. Individualized Academic Planning - Set realistic targets for GPA, course rigor, and relevant qualifications such as SAT, IELTS, AP, IB, IGCSE, or A-Level, depending on the student's curriculum and target universities.
 
 3. Specialized Academic Support - Connect students with suitable GSJ academic programs and experienced instructors for advanced subject learning and examination preparation.
 
 4. Progress Monitoring & Adjustment - Review academic milestones regularly and refine the learning plan to maintain progress without unnecessary overload.
 
 Outcome: A stronger academic profile aligned with the student's capabilities and target university requirements.
Turn your interests into meaningful achievements.

Academic results demonstrate what students can achieve in the classroom. Meaningful experiences reveal how they apply their knowledge, take initiative, solve problems, and contribute beyond it.
 
 MIT's admissions guidance encourages students to “Choose quality over quantity.” The university values genuine enthusiasm and sustained commitment over simply accumulating activities.
 
 Harvard likewise recognizes students who demonstrate exceptional ability in a particular area, as well as those whose broader contributions reflect their character and potential.

Students often participate in numerous clubs, competitions, or volunteer activities without a clear purpose. Some lack access to research mentors, meaningful projects, or opportunities to demonstrate their interests through tangible outcomes.

Step 1: Build a Strategic Activity Portfolio
Evaluate existing experiences and identify a focused combination of research, competitions, leadership, community engagement, and personal projects aligned with the student's interests.
 
Step 2: Engage in Specialized Research
Develop research questions, learn scientific methods, collect and analyze data, and communicate findings with guidance from GSJ research mentors and relevant specialists.
 
Step 3: Pursue Academic Competitions & Challenges
Receive guidance and preparation for suitable national and international competitions in science, engineering, technology, business, and other relevant disciplines.
 
Step 4: Develop Leadership & Passion Projects
Transform personal interests into student-led initiatives, entrepreneurial projects, or community-focused activities with measurable goals and meaningful impact.
 
Step 5: Reflect, Document & Demonstrate Growth
Help students evaluate lessons learned, document their contributions, and communicate the impact of their work through portfolios, presentations, and activity descriptions.
 
Outcome: An authentic extracurricular portfolio demonstrating intellectual curiosity, initiative, sustained commitment, and personal growth.

Find the right university, not just the highest-ranked one.

A university's ranking alone cannot determine whether it is the right fit. Academic offerings, learning environment, financial considerations, career opportunities, and personal aspirations all influence a student's long-term success.
 
 Yale emphasizes reviewing applicants in the context of their opportunities and experiences, illustrating why students should approach university selection with an understanding of both institutional expectations and their own circumstances.
Students and families may struggle to compare universities beyond rankings, estimate the true cost of attendance, understand scholarship policies, or develop a balanced application list.

1. Profile & Goal Alignment: Revisit academic interests, career ambitions, achievements, budget, and preferred study destinations.
 2. University Research & Shortlisting: Evaluate institutions based on program fit, admissions requirements, campus environment, career opportunities, and affordability.
 3. Admissions & Scholarship Strategy: Develop a balanced university list and assess relevant scholarships, financial aid options, and application rounds.
 4. Personalized Application Timeline: Establish key deadlines, responsibilities, and milestones for each target institution.
 
 Outcome: A well-researched university shortlist and an application strategy grounded in personal fit and realistic priorities.
Bring your story to life - authentically and convincingly.
An application is more than a record of achievements. Essays, recommendations, and interviews provide admissions committees with insights into the person behind the numbers.

Students may find it difficult to identify meaningful stories, articulate their motivations, or present their achievements without sounding generic. Managing multiple essays, documents, recommendation requests, and deadlines also requires careful coordination.

1. Personal Story Discovery: Use reflective conversations to identify defining experiences, personal values, motivations, and lessons learned.
2. Essay Planning & Coaching: Guide students through brainstorming, structuring, drafting, and revising personal statements and university-specific essays while preserving their authentic voices.
3. Application Documentation: Support the organization and review of application forms, activity lists, CVs, portfolios, and recommendation request materials.
4. Interview Preparation: Practice communicating academic interests, experiences, future ambitions, and personal perspectives through mock interviews and targeted feedback.
5. Final Review & Submission Support: Check application completeness, coordinate timelines, and support students in submitting materials by the relevant deadlines.
 
Outcome: A complete, carefully prepared application that communicates the student's strengths and individual story.
Our commitment does not end with an acceptance letter.

Receiving university offers is a major milestone, but choosing where to enroll and preparing for life overseas are equally important decisions.
 
Students must consider financial commitments, visa procedures, housing, cultural adjustment, and the expectations of university-level study.
Students and families may feel uncertain when comparing offers, preparing immigration documents, organizing travel, or adapting to an unfamiliar academic and social environment.

1. Offer & Financial Aid Review: Compare admission offers, available scholarships, estimated costs, and academic opportunities to support informed decisions.
 
2. Enrollment & Visa Preparation: Guide students through enrollment requirements, visa documentation preparation, and interview practice where applicable.
 
3. Pre-Departure Orientation: Provide guidance on academic expectations, cultural adaptation, independent living, and practical preparations for studying overseas.
 
4. Community & Transition Support: Help students connect with relevant resources and communities as they prepare for their new environment.
 
Outcome: Greater confidence and readiness to begin university life abroad.
More Than Admissions Consultants. Your Partners in Growth.
What makes GSJ different is not simply how we help students apply to universities, but how we help them become stronger candidates long before they apply.

Personalized, Long-Term Mentorship
 
No two students share the same ambitions, strengths, or starting points. GSJ develops individualized roadmaps with clear milestones, ongoing progress reviews, and close collaboration among students, mentors, and parents.

Learning by Doing, Not Just Planning
 
Our philosophy, Learn for Real. Do for Real., goes beyond conventional admissions counseling. Through GSJ's educational programs, students have opportunities to put knowledge into practice, explore their interests, and develop tangible projects and experiences.

Specialized Academic & Industry Expertise
 
GSJ connects students with experienced educators, researchers, and subject specialists across science, technology, engineering, business, and other disciplines, helping them explore academic interests with greater depth and practical understanding.

International Competition Experience
 
GSJ has supported student teams participating in international science, innovation, and business competitions, including iCAN, iWISE, AI-JAM, INOVA Croatia, IBO, BBO, JCOO, 1I1W, GYS, Asia Business Simulation (ABS),... These experiences inform our approach to developing students' research capabilities, teamwork, strategic thinking, and presentation skills.

Integrated Student - Mentor - Parent Partnership
 
We believe sustainable progress requires more than occasional counseling sessions. GSJ brings students, mentors, and parents together through structured planning, regular communication, and continuous support, keeping everyone aligned throughout the preparation journey.
We Don’t Just Help Students Build Applications. We Help Them Build the Experiences Behind Them.
